ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that point $E$ is located on the side $AB$ of the square $ABCD$. A square $BEFG$ is constructed outside square $ABCD$ with $E$ as one of its sides. Line segments $DF$ and $MN$ are drawn, where $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $DC$ and $DF$, respectively. If $AB=7$ and $BE=5$, what is the length of $MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line CF, \\
$\because$ In square ABCD and square BEFG, we have AB=7, BE=5, \\
$\therefore$ GF=GB=5, BC=7, \\
$\therefore$ GC=GB+BC=5+7=12, \\
$\therefore$ CF= $\sqrt{GF^{2}+GC^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}=13$, \\
$\because$ M and N are the midpoints of DC and DF respectively, \\
$\therefore$ MN= $\frac{1}{2}$ CF= $\boxed{\frac{13}{2}}$;

Image description: On the right side of the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; E is on side AB. On the left side, with BE as one side, square BEFG is constructed outward, F is on the left side of E, G is on the left side of B, and G, B, C are on the same straight line. DF is drawn in the figure, M is on DC, N is on DF, and the problem gives that M, N are respectively the midpoints of DC, DF.

Reasoning: Because ABCD is a square and AB=7, BC=7. Because BEFG is a square and BE=5, BG=GF=5. From the figure it can be seen that G, B, C are collinear, therefore GC=GB+BC=5+7=12. Consider line segment CF, triangle GCF is right-angled at G, so CF=sqrt(GF^2+GC^2)=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=13. In triangle DCF, M is the midpoint of DC, N is the midpoint of DF, therefore MN is the midline of triangle DCF, MN=CF/2=13/2.
